events.region: Winthrop Harbor to Wilmette Harbor IL; Lake Michigan from Winthrop Harbor to Wilmette Harbor IL 5NM offshore to Mid Lake
events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
SMWLOT

The National Weather Service in Chicago has issued a

* Special Marine Warning for...

Nearshore Waters from Winthrop Harbor to Wilmette Harbor...
Open Waters from Winthrop Harbor to Wilmette Harbor out to Mid
Lake...

* Until 1245 PM CDT.

* At 1119 AM CDT, a severe thunderstorm was located near Wilmette
Harbor, moving east at 20 knots.

HAZARD...Wind gusts 34 knots or greater and large hail.

SOURCE...Radar.

IMPACT...Small craft could be damaged in briefly higher winds and
suddenly higher waves. Large hail could result in
structural damage.

* The severe thunderstorm will remain over mainly open waters.

Island, or near Algonac, moving east at 35 mph.

Center, Fraser, Utica, Smiths Creek, and Eastpointe.

* Flash Flood Warning for...

Redland, Marquez, Leona, Pleasant Springs, Flo, Eunice, Robbins,
Centerview and Flynn.

events.region: Lake; Geauga; Ashtabula Inland; Trumbull; Ashtabula Lakeshore; Northern Erie; Southern Erie; Crawford
events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
* WHAT...Flash flooding caused by excessive rainfall is possible.

* WHERE...Portions of northeast Ohio, including the following areas,
Ashtabula Inland, Ashtabula Lakeshore, Geauga, Lake and Trumbull
and northwest Pennsylvania, including the following areas,
Crawford, Northern Erie and Southern Erie.

* WHEN...Through this evening.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.
Low-water crossings may be flooded.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Heavy rain has fallen over the watch area over the last 24 hours.
Additional showers and thunderstorms are expected later today
which could produce locally heavy rainfall of 1 to 3 inches.
These repeated rounds of rain could result in flooding of urban
corridors along with flooding of streams, creeks, and other low
lying areas.
- Please visit www.weather.gov/safety/flood for flood safety and
preparedness information.

events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
...HIGH SURF ADVISORY FOR SOUTH AND SOUTHEAST FACING SHORES
THROUGH THURSDAY NIGHT...

.Swells from Hurricane Lowell will steadily fill in across rest
of the island chain today and will produce advisory level surf
for south and southeast exposures throughout the state. Swells
from Lowell will gradually veer from southeast to south as well.
Additionally, a moderate long period south swell will gradually
decline through the rest of the week.

* WHAT...Large breaking waves up to 10 feet.

* WHERE...South and southeast exposures of all Hawaiian Islands.

* WHEN...Until 6 AM HST Friday.

* IMPACTS...Moderate. Strong breaking waves and strong currents
will make swimming dangerous.
